newsitem.title: USA: Hurricane Fran moves toward Bahamas, southern U.S.
newsitem.headline: Hurricane Fran moves toward Bahamas, southern U.S.

text.p: A hurricane watch was issued for the Bahamas on Tuesday as Hurricane Fran moved toward Nassau and the southeastern United States, forecasters at the National Hurricane Center said here.
Fran threatens the Bahamas and could reach the southeastern Atlantic U.S. coast by late on Thursday, said meteorologist Martin Nelson.

At 5 a.m. EDT (0900 GMT) the storm was 420 miles (675 km) east of Nassau and 500 miles (800 km) east-southeast of Miami. Its 80 mph (130 kph) winds were moving west-northwest at 13 mph (19 kph), Nelson said.
The Bahamian government issued a hurricane watch for the central portion of the 600-mile (965-km) long archipelego, including the islands of San Salvador, Great Exuma, Long Islnd and Cat Island.
"We expect Fran to be 200 miles (320 km) east of Cape Canaveral on Thursday morning.... It could make landfall in Georgia or South Carolina late on Thursday or early on Friday," according to Nelson.
However, he said there could be major variations in Fran's track, based on changing conditions.
Hurricane-force winds extended outward about 60 miles (95 km) from Fran's center.

In central Florida, the U.S. space agency said it would decide on Tuesday whether to move the shuttle Atlantis off its seaside launch pad. Atlantis is being prepared for a Sept. 14 launch to rendezvous with the Russian space station and pick up American astronaut Shannon Lucid.
